renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: allele_dot_plot
  title: Binding by allele and sample
  description: |-
    Each dot is an HLA allele in one sample: its size is the share of peptides that at least one tool calls a binder and its colour is the median affinity score of the peptides. It answers which alleles present the most candidate peptides.
    How to read: a large, strongly coloured dot is an allele with many predicted binders of good affinity, so its peptides are the first to follow up. Small pale dots are alleles that bind few of the peptides. A column that stands apart from the others in size points to a sample with a different peptide set or tool mix.
    Lines and annotations: the binder call is the one the pipeline writes for each tool, a percentile rank of 2 or less for MHCflurry, NetMHCpan and MixMHCpred, 5 or less for NetMHCIIpan, and an affinity score of at least 0.425 (500 nM) for MHCnuggets. The affinity score is 1 minus log10 of the IC50 over log10 of 50000.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: allele
    mean_expression: median_affinity_score
    frac_expressing: binder_rate

- component: card
  id: allele_binders
  title: Predicted binders
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of binder peptides over every allele and sample in view, and the bars rank the HLA loci by their share. It answers how many candidate peptides the alleles present and through which locus.
    How to read: a locus that carries most binders is the one the patient's peptides fit best. The compact line gives the median and the largest binder count of one allele, so a total spread over many alleles reads differently from one dominant allele. Binders are the tools' own calls, see the dot plot for the rules.
  column: binders
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: hla_locus
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: binders, by HLA locus

- component: card
  id: allele_binder_rate
  title: Binder share per allele
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of scored peptides that a tool calls a binder, over the alleles in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how selective the alleles are.
    How to read: a low median with a few high alleles is the usual pattern, since few peptides bind any one allele. A box shifted high means a peptide set enriched for binders, for example after a binder filter, or permissive tools. Filter to one sample to compare alleles within it.
  column: binder_rate
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: binder share, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Binders per allele
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of binder peptides for an allele, split by sample. It answers which alleles contribute the most candidates and whether samples agree.
    How to read: tall bars mark alleles that bind many peptides. An allele that is tall in one sample only reflects that sample's peptide set, not the allele alone. Pick a locus in the filter to narrow the alleles.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: allele
    y: binders
    color: sample
    labels:
      allele: Allele
      binders: Binder peptides
      sample: Sample

- component: interactive
  title: HLA locus
  description: Pick one or more HLA loci to restrict the dot plot, the cards and the table to them. It answers
    how a single locus behaves.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: hla_locus

- component: table
  title: Allele binding table
  description: |-
    Each row is an allele in one sample with its peptide count, binder count and share, and the median and best IC50. It answers the exact numbers behind the plots and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by binders or by best IC50 to find the alleles worth following up.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: allele_key

- component: card
  id: peptide_count
  title: Peptides scored
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of sample and peptide rows, the compact line gives the distinct sequences, and the bar splits the rows into binder, non-binder and not scored. It answers how many peptides went through prediction and how many a tool could score.
    How to read: a large not-scored share means the alleles or peptide lengths are outside what the tools support. A binder share far above a few percent suggests a binder filter was applied upstream. Calls are the pipeline's own, a percentile rank of 2 or less for most tools and an IC50 of 500 nM or less for MHCnuggets.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: call
  caption: peptides, by call
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: binder_count
  title: Binder peptides
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of peptides that at least one tool calls a binder, the compact line gives the distinct sequences, and the bar splits them by peptide length. It answers how many candidates remain and which lengths dominate.
    How to read: the lengths come from the run's minimum and maximum peptide length settings, so a length with no binders may simply be a length the tools score poorly. Binders are the pipeline's own calls, see the Peptides scored tile.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: length_class
  filter_expr: col('binder') == 1
  caption: binders, by peptide length
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: binding_alleles
  title: Alleles bound per binder
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of alleles a binder peptide binds, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether binders are allele-specific or promiscuous.
    How to read: a median of one means most peptides fit a single allele. Peptides that bind several alleles are more likely to be presented in the patient and are good candidates to prioritise.
  column: binding_alleles
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  filter_expr: col('binder') == 1
  caption: alleles bound, distribution

- component: card
  id: peptide_length
  title: Peptide length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median peptide length in residues and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether the peptide set matches the MHC class that was scored.
    How to read: the lengths are set by the run's minimum and maximum peptide length options for each MHC class, and each tool has its own fixed range. A wide spread shows a run that scored both classes.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/usage.md
  column: length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: peptide length, distribution

- component: figure
  id: length_by_class
  title: Calls by peptide length
  description: |-
    Each bar counts peptides of one length, stacked by binder call and split by MHC class. It answers which lengths yield binders.
    How to read: a length with many peptides and no binders is mostly noise, and a length with a high binder share is where to look first. Lengths outside a tool's supported range are not scored by it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/usage.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length_class
    color: call
    facet_col: mhc_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      length_class: Peptide length
      call: Call
      mhc_class: MHC class
      count: Peptides

- component: figure
  title: Calls per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the peptides of a sample, stacked by call. It answers how big each peptide set is and how its calls split.
    How to read: compare the binder share across samples. A sample with far more not-scored peptides used alleles or lengths that the tools do not support.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    color: call
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      call: Call
      count: Peptides

- component: interactive
  title: Call
  description: Pick binder, non-binder or not scored to restrict the cards, the plots and the table to those
    peptides. It answers what a single call looks like.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: call

- component: interactive
  title: Peptide length
  description: Pick one or more peptide lengths to restrict the tiles to them. It answers how binders behave
    at one length.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: length_class

- component: table
  title: Peptide table
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptide in a sample with its best prediction over all alleles and tools, the number of alleles it binds and its source gene and protein change for variant input. It answers which peptides to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by best IC50 or by the number of binding alleles, and filter to mutant peptides to see the neoepitope candidates.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peptide_key

- component: advanced_viz
  id: affinity_rank_scatter
  title: IC50 against percentile rank
  description: |-
    Each point is one prediction of a peptide against an allele: its predicted IC50 on the horizontal axis and its percentile rank on the vertical axis, coloured by the tool. It answers whether a tool's affinity and rank agree and where its binder call falls.
    How to read: a lower IC50 and a lower rank both mean stronger binding, so confident binders sit at the lower left. A tool whose points form a clear edge has a rank cut-off that decides its binder call. A tool with no IC50 does not appear here.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line is 500 nM, an IC50 below which peptides are usually considered binders. The binder call of each tool uses its own rank rule, a rank of 2 or less for MHCflurry, NetMHCpan and MixMHCpred, 5 or less for NetMHCIIpan.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Predicted IC50 (nM)
    y_title: Percentile rank
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    reference_line: vertical
    reference_value: 500
    reference_label: 500 nM, usual binder limit
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: ic50_nm
    y: percentile_rank
    label: sequence
    color: predictor

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mutant_wildtype_scatter
  title: Mutant against wild-type IC50
  description: |-
    Each point is a mutant peptide predicted against an allele: the IC50 of its wild type on the horizontal axis and its own IC50 on the vertical axis, coloured by allele. It answers whether the mutation changes binding.
    How to read: points below the diagonal bind more strongly than their wild type and are the neoepitope candidates, especially when the wild type is above the binder limit. Points on the diagonal are unchanged. Only missense peptides with a predicted wild type appear.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is where the mutant and wild-type IC50 are equal, an identity line and not a cut-off. A mutant IC50 below 500 nM is usually considered a binder.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Wild-type IC50 (nM)
    y_title: Mutant IC50 (nM)
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Mutant equals wild type
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: wt_ic50_nm
    y: ic50_nm
    label: sequence
    color: allele

- component: figure
  title: Distribution of predicted IC50
  description: |-
    Each bar counts predictions in a log10 IC50 bin, overlaid by tool. It answers how the tools spread their affinities and where most peptides fall.
    How to read: most peptides are weak or non-binders, so the mass sits above 3 (1000 nM). A value of 2.7 is 500 nM, the usual binder limit, and 1.7 is 50 nM, a strong binder. A tool with a very different shape scores on another scale, so compare calls rather than raw values.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median log10 IC50 of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/epitopeprediction.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: log10_ic50
    color: predictor
    barmode: overlay
    labels:
      log10_ic50: Log10 IC50 (nM)
      predictor: Tool
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: log10_ic50

- component: card
  id: prediction_count
  title: Predictions made
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of predictions, one per peptide, allele and tool, the compact line gives the distinct peptides, and the ring splits them by tool. It answers how much scoring was done and how it is shared between tools.
    How to read: a tool with a small share scored fewer peptides because of the alleles or lengths it supports. The same peptide scored by several tools counts once per tool.
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: predictor
  caption: predictions, by tool
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: binder_calls
  title: Binder calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of predictions that a tool calls a binder, the compact line gives the distinct peptides, and the bar splits them by HLA locus. It answers how many predictions pass and through which locus.
    How to read: a peptide called a binder by several tools or alleles counts several times here, so the distinct count is the number of candidates. Binder calls are the pipeline's own, a percentile rank of 2 or less for most tools.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: hla_locus
  filter_expr: col('binder') == 1
  caption: binder calls, by HLA locus

- component: card
  id: allele_count
  title: Alleles scored
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct alleles scored, the compact line gives the most frequent one, and the bars rank the HLA loci by how many alleles they have. It answers how wide the typing is.
    How to read: a lower count than expected means a homozygous or partial typing. A locus missing here was not scored at all.
  column: allele
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: hla_locus
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: alleles, by HLA locus
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: median_ic50
  title: Median predicted IC50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median predicted IC50 in nM over every prediction in view, compared with a cut-off. It answers whether the typical peptide is a binder.
    How to read: most peptides do not bind, so a median above the limit is the normal case. A median below it means a peptide set already enriched for binders. The compact line gives the best and worst IC50.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is 500 nM, an IC50 below which peptides are usually considered binders.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  column: ic50_nm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 500.0
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: median IC50 against the 500 nM binder limit

- component: interactive
  title: Allele
  description: Pick one or more alleles to restrict the plots, the cards and the table to them. It answers
    how a single allele scores.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: allele

- component: interactive
  title: Prediction tool
  description: Pick one or more tools to restrict the tiles to them. It answers how one tool scores on its
    own.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: predictor

- component: interactive
  title: Log10 IC50
  description: Drag the range to keep predictions within a log10 IC50 window. It answers which peptides
    fall in a chosen affinity band, for example 1.7 to 2.7 for binders between 50 and 500 nM.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: log10_ic50

- component: table
  title: Binding prediction table
  description: |-
    Each row is one prediction of a peptide against an allele by a tool, with its affinity score, IC50, percentile rank, binder call and class. It answers the exact values behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by IC50 or percentile rank and filter to one allele or tool to follow up the strongest candidates.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: row_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: agreement_scatter
  title: IC50 of one tool against another
  description: |-
    Each point is a peptide scored against an allele by two tools: the IC50 of the first on the horizontal axis and of the second on the vertical axis, coloured by whether both, neither or only one calls a binder. It answers how consistent the tools are.
    How to read: points on the diagonal get the same affinity from both tools. Points far from it, or coloured as one tool only, are peptides whose call depends on the tool and should be confirmed before they are trusted.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is where the two IC50 are equal, an identity line and not a cut-off. Binder calls are each tool's own rule, a percentile rank of 2 or less for most tools and an IC50 of 500 nM or less for MHCnuggets.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: IC50 of the first tool (nM)
    y_title: IC50 of the second tool (nM)
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Both tools agree
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: ic50_a_nm
    y: ic50_b_nm
    label: sequence
    color: agreement

- component: card
  id: paired_predictions
  title: Tool pairs compared
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of peptide, allele and tool-pair rows, the compact line gives the distinct peptides, and the bar splits them by outcome. It answers how often the tools agree.
    How to read: a large share where neither tool calls a binder is normal, since most peptides do not bind. The share where only one tool calls a binder is the part that needs a second opinion.
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: agreement
  caption: pairs, by agreement

- component: card
  id: ic50_gap
  title: Typical IC50 gap
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median absolute log10 ratio between the two tools' IC50, and the histogram shows the distribution. A value of 1 is a ten-fold difference. It answers how far apart the tools are on a typical peptide.
    How to read: a median near zero means the tools agree on the scale. A median of one or more means they score on different scales, so compare binder calls and not raw IC50 values.
  column: abs_log10_ratio
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q3
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: IC50 gap, distribution

- component: card
  id: disputed_binders
  title: Disputed binder calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of pairs where exactly one tool calls a binder, the compact line gives the distinct peptides, and the bar shows which tool is the caller. It answers how many candidates depend on the choice of tool.
    How to read: a disputed pair is not wrong, since the tools use different rank rules, but its peptide is a weaker candidate than one that every tool calls. Check the scatter to see how far apart the IC50 values are.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: agreement
  filter_expr: col('concordant') == 0
  caption: disputed pairs, by who calls a binder

- component: interactive
  title: Agreement
  description: Pick an outcome, both, neither or one tool only, to restrict the scatter, the cards and the
    table to it. It answers what the disputed peptides look like.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: agreement

- component: table
  title: Tool agreement table
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptide and allele scored by two tools, with both IC50, their log10 ratio, both binder calls and the outcome. It answers the exact values behind the scatter and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by the absolute log ratio to find the largest disagreements.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: pair_key

- component: figure
  id: binder_rate_bar
  title: Binder share per tool
  description: |-
    Each bar is the share of a tool's scored peptides that it calls a binder, grouped by sample. It answers how permissive each tool is on the same peptides.
    How to read: tools use different rules, a percentile rank of 2 or less for most and an IC50 of 500 nM or less for MHCnuggets, so their shares are not directly comparable. A tool far above the others in every sample is the most permissive. Wild-type peptides are left out, as in the pipeline's own statistics.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median binder share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/epitopeprediction.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: binder_rate
    color: predictor
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      binder_rate: Binder share
      predictor: Tool
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: binder_rate

- component: card
  id: tool_binders
  title: Binders per tool
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of binder peptides over the tools and samples in view, and the ring splits them by tool. It answers which tool contributes the most candidates.
    How to read: a tool with a large slice is permissive or scored more peptides. The compact line gives the median and the highest count of one tool and sample.
  column: binders
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: predictor
  caption: binders, by tool

- component: card
  id: tool_unsupported
  title: Peptides a tool could not score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of peptides that a tool could not score because of an unsupported allele or length, and the bar splits them by tool. It answers how much of the input each tool leaves out.
    How to read: a tool that leaves out many peptides covers less of the input, so its binder count understates the candidates. Check the supported alleles and lengths in the pipeline's usage notes.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/usage.md
  column: unsupported
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: predictor
  caption: unscored peptides, by tool

- component: card
  title: Binder share per tool and sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median binder share over the tool and sample rows in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers what share of scored peptides a tool usually calls a binder.
    How to read: a low median is expected, since few peptides bind any allele. A wide box shows tools or samples that differ strongly, so open the bar chart to see which.
  column: binder_rate
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: binder share, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Prediction tool
  description: Pick one or more tools to restrict the bars, the cards and the table to them. It answers
    how one tool behaves.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: predictor

- component: table
  title: Tool summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a tool in a sample with the peptides it was given, scored, could not score and called binders, its binder share, the alleles scored and its median IC50. It answers the exact numbers behind the tiles and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: compare scored with unsupported counts before comparing binder shares.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: summary_key

- component: figure
  id: consequence_bar
  title: Candidate peptides by consequence
  description: |-
    Each bar counts candidate peptides for one variant consequence, stacked by peptide length. It answers which kinds of variant yield the peptides to score.
    How to read: a frameshift or in-frame indel produces many peptides from one variant, because every peptide that overlaps the changed sequence counts, so a tall bar does not mean many variants. Missense variants are the only ones with a wild-type counterpart.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: consequence
    color: length_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      consequence: Variant consequence
      length_class: Peptide length
      count: Candidate peptides

- component: card
  id: variant_count
  title: Variants represented
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct variant positions that yielded peptides, the compact line gives the number of peptide rows, and the bars rank the consequences by their variants. It answers how many variants feed the prediction.
    How to read: a large gap between peptide rows and variants means a few variants, often frameshifts, contribute most of the peptides.
  column: genomic_anchor
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: consequence
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: variants, by consequence

- component: card
  id: candidate_count
  title: Candidate peptides
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of candidate peptide rows, the compact line gives the distinct sequences, and the bar splits them by variant consequence. It answers how many peptides go to the predictors.
    How to read: the same sequence can come from several samples or variants, so the distinct count is the number of different peptides to score. Wild-type peptides added by the wild-type option are counted here as well.
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: consequence
  caption: peptides, by consequence

- component: interactive
  title: Variant consequence
  description: Pick one or more consequences to restrict the bars, the cards and the table to them. It answers
    what a single kind of variant contributes.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: consequence

- component: table
  title: Variant peptide table
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate peptide with its gene, transcript, consequence, protein change, genomic position and UniProt accession. It answers which variant each peptide comes from and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: filter to mutant peptides of one gene to review its variants.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peptide_key

- component: advanced_viz
  id: wildtype_scatter
  title: Mutant against wild-type IC50
  description: |-
    Each point is a missense mutant peptide against an allele and a tool: the IC50 of its wild type on the horizontal axis and its own IC50 on the vertical axis, coloured by the outcome. It answers which mutations create or strengthen binding.
    How to read: points below the diagonal bind more strongly than their wild type. The classic neoepitope candidate is a mutant binder whose wild type does not bind. Points on the diagonal are unchanged by the mutation.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is where the mutant and wild-type IC50 are equal, an identity line and not a cut-off. Binder calls are each tool's own rule, a percentile rank of 2 or less for most tools and an IC50 of 500 nM or less for MHCnuggets.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/epitopeprediction/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Wild-type IC50 (nM)
    y_title: Mutant IC50 (nM)
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Mutant equals wild type
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: wt_ic50_nm
    y: ic50_nm
    label: sequence
    color: pair_call

- component: card
  id: pair_outcomes
  title: Mutant and wild-type pairs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of mutant and wild-type pairs, the compact line gives the distinct mutant peptides, and the bar splits them by outcome. It answers how many mutations change binding.
    How to read: the share where the mutant binds and the wild type does not is the candidate list. A large share where neither binds is common, since most peptides do not bind.
  column: sequence
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: pair_call
  caption: pairs, by outcome

- component: card
  id: agretopicity_median
  title: Change in affinity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log10 agretopicity, which is the log10 of the mutant IC50 over the wild-type IC50, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how strongly mutations change binding.
    How to read: a value below zero means the mutant binds more strongly than its wild type and a value above zero less strongly. A box centred on zero means most mutations leave binding unchanged, and the hero is a range and not a median because a median over both directions cancels out.
  column: log10_agretopicity
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: log10 agretopicity, quartiles

- component: interactive
  title: Outcome
  description: Pick an outcome, for example a mutant binder whose wild type does not bind, to restrict the
    scatter, the cards and the table to it. It answers what the candidates look like.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: pair_call

- component: table
  title: Mutant and wild-type table
  description: |-
    Each row is a mutant peptide with its wild type, allele and tool, both IC50, both binder calls, the agretopicity and the outcome. It answers the exact values behind the scatter and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: filter to the outcome where only the mutant binds and sort by mutant IC50 to rank the candidates.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: pair_key
